You are reviewing the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim (branch llamacpp) for STRUCTURAL refactor candidates.
First read /home/nick/work/andesim/CLAUDE.md to understand the architecture.

HARD RULES:
- READ-ONLY. Do not edit, build, or run anything (no make, no scripts, no ./andesim). Baseline test runs are using the build tree right now. Use Read/Grep/Glob and read-only git commands only.
- Structural = behavior-preserving: dead code, duplication, needless complexity, stale comments/docs that contradict the code, naming that hides intent, repo hygiene. NOT rewrites for taste. The repo just went through a history cleanup, so it is fairly clean; report only what you can defend with evidence. An empty findings list is a valid answer.
- If you find what looks like a real BUG (behavior wrong), report it with category "bug-report" - it will be handled separately, not as a refactor.
- For every finding give: file (repo-relative), line, category, title, one-paragraph detail with EVIDENCE (what you read/grepped), safety (why removing/changing it cannot change behavior), verify_with (which existing test or check proves it after the change).
- Cite real file paths and line numbers you actually read. No speculation.

Your assigned scope (do not wander into other subsystems except to grep for references):
runtime/linux/ (the new vlinux proxy kernel from commit cf8a7ee): syscall.c (693 lines), stack.c, loader.c, mm.c, main.c, vlinux.ld. This is the newest code - look for copy-paste from runtime/ top level, dead debug scaffolding, magic numbers that duplicate constants defined elsewhere.

Return your findings as the structured output.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.

Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.

BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

6	/* Set the brk arena's floor (the app's own image end -- loaded_elf.image_end)
7	 * and the mmap arena's ceiling (mem_size minus stack.h's 8 MiB stack
8	 * reservation -- "just below the app stack", the roadmap's guest memory
9	 * map). Must be called once, before any sys_brk/sys_mmap call. */
10	void mm_init(uint64_t app_image_end, uint64_t mem_size);

12	/* The manifest's guest RAM size, for sys_sysinfo's totalram/freeram. */
13	uint64_t mm_total_ram(void);
14	
15	/* brk(2): addr==0 queries the current break; otherwise tries to set it.
16	 * Linux syscall convention: always returns the RESULTING break (old value
17	 * on failure, not -1) -- glibc's brk() wrapper compares it against what it
18	 * asked for. */
19	long sys_brk(unsigned long addr);
20	
21	/* mmap(2): bump-allocates from the top of the mmap arena downward.
22	 * MAP_ANONYMOUS is zeroed (the POSIX guarantee); `addr` is ignored (no
23	 * MAP_FIXED support). MAP_PRIVATE file-backed (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md
24	 * U7, llama.cpp's default GGUF load path): the [offset, offset+length)
25	 * range is eagerly read (htif_pread) into the freshly-allocated arena
26	 * space -- a real, private, independently-owned COPY, which is exactly
27	 * what MAP_PRIVATE promises (writes never propagate back to the file;
28	 * there is simply nowhere for this relay to route them even if it wanted
29	 * to). MAP_SHARED is not supported (-ENOSYS): this relay has no way to
30	 * write a shared mapping's changes back to the host file. Returns a
31	 * negative errno on failure, matching the raw syscall (not the libc
32	 * wrapper's -1 + errno) convention. */
33	long sys_mmap(unsigned long addr, unsigned long length, long prot,
34	             long flags, long fd, long offset);
35	
36	/* munmap(2)/mprotect(2): the bump allocator never reclaims or changes
37	 * protection (there is no MMU here -- every page is already RWX), so both
38	 * are accepted no-ops for ANY address/length, mapped or not -- POSIX
39	 * itself allows this (munmap(2): "it is not an error if the indicated
40	 * range does not contain any mapped pages"), so llama.cpp's partial
41	 * unmap of an unused GGUF tail range is answered correctly without
42	 * needing to track individual mappings. A real munmap would let the
43	 * arena run out sooner than it should; that is a leak, not a crash. */
44	long sys_munmap(unsigned long addr, unsigned long length);
45	long sys_mprotect(unsigned long addr, unsigned long length, long prot);

49	 * a caller (llama.cpp does not use this for GGUF loading) gets a loud,
50	 * correct failure instead of silent corruption. */

10	 * and no guest-side CCTL sequence can fix that (the VA-scoped forms trap
11	 * on RVH cores, the ALL forms drop unrelated dirty lines).

13	 *   stdio (fd 0-2)  ATCUART100 UART2: THR @0xf0300020, LSR @0xf0300034.

16	 *                   @0xe0080028. Served host-side (vsim: sim_control.hpp

4	# crt0.S's cache/FS/VS/UNA bring-up and the HTIF UART/exit stubs use only
5	# PC-relative addressing and a linker-provided _stack symbol, so the same
6	# object already works at vlinux's load address (0x0200_0000) with no
7	# vlinux-specific fork. main.c (banner + manifest), vlinux.ld (link base +
8	# .manifest section), loader.c (ELF read + PT_LOAD mapping), stack.c (Linux
9	# initial stack + auxv), mm.c (brk/mmap arenas) and syscall.c (the app's
10	# ecall dispatch, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U3/U4) are vlinux-specific.
11	#
12	# Output: ../../build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf
13	
14	TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
15	TRIPLE    := riscv64-unknown-elf
16	CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/$(TRIPLE)-gcc
17	
18	ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
19	$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh`, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path)

28	# U9's loader.c overlap check) -- C and C++ both compile it (see the header's
29	# own comment); already included the same way by qemu_plugin/Makefile.
30	HYBRID_INCLUDE := ../../include
31

33	
34	all: $(OUT)/vlinux.elf

36	$(OUT):
37		mkdir -p $@
38	
39	# The shared runtime lib + crt0.o (make -C .. is a fast no-op when
40	# already up to date, so this always runs rather than duplicating
41	# runtime/'s own source-file dependency list here).
42	rtlib:
43		$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

45	SRCS := main.c loader.c stack.c mm.c syscall.c
46	HDRS := manifest.h loader.h stack.h mm.h ../ecall_hook.h \
47	        $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi.h
